en: Oṃ, salutations to the venerable gurus; [salutations to] the sandals.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ, the sandal of the infinite knot.
At the two feet: Aiṃ Śhrīṃ Śrīṃ Hāṃ, the sandals of Kālagranthi.
At both ankles: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hīṃ, the Rudra-knot, the venerable sandals.
To the two shanks: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hīṃ, the venerable sandals of the Jyeṣṭha-knot.
On the two thighs: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, the venerable sandals of the left knot.
On the two hips: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hūṃ, the venerable sandals of Kāmagranthi.
In front of the *liṅga*: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrūṃ, the *śrīpādukā* of the *piṇḍagranthi*.
At the base of the *liṅga*: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hṛṃ, the *śrīpādukā* of the Brahmagranthi.
O Jāṭhala! Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hḷṃ, [I worship] the venerable sandals of Sūryagranthi.
At the navel: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hḷṃ, the lunar knot, the venerable sandals.
At the half of the navel: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ, the *śrīpādukā* of the *prāṇa-granthi*.
In the stomach: Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Haiṁ, the *śrīpādukā* of the *jīvagranthi*.
In the heart: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hoṃ, the venerable sandals of the Viṣṇu-knot.
At the throat: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hauṃ, the venerable sandals of Raudragranthi.
At the region of the palate: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ, the Īśvara-granthi, the venerable pādukā.
At the head: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haḥ, the *śrīpādukā* of the Sadāśiva-knot.
In the region of the head.
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) for the knot of the glorious Vajrakavaca.
Having touched the knot with the *nyāsa* and recited the *yoni-mantra*,
when great danger has arisen, there is no doubt for one who possesses a body of adamant.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ, I worship the sandals of the venerable Guru.

In the Hotṛ’s area, facing north, one should construct a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) according to the specific desired object— whether triangular, hexagonal, square, or circular— adorned with serpents, provided with three girdles (mekhalā), endowed with the yoni and other features, and possessing all the required characteristics.
Having smeared [the ground] with a paste of red sandalwood and other ingredients— such as musk, saffron, and white sandalwood— ground together with a mixture of heroic ashes.

Having sipped water three times (*trimācamya*), [perform] the *sūryārgha* (offering to the Sun), *prāṇāyāma* (breath control), the *nyāsakara-nyāsa* (the ritual placement of the hands), and the *mūla-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa* (the six-limbed placement with the root mantra). Perform the *bhūtaśuddhi* (purification of the elements). Having performed the binding of the ten directions with unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) using the mantra "Oṃ Hūṃ apasarppantu... and so forth, perform the worship of the water vessel (*jalapātrapūjā*).
The worship of the argha vessel: With these substances, everything is offered. For the sake of self-worship.
For the consecration of the sacrificial fire-pit.
Alternatively, one should purify the winds by means of the four [practices] beginning with visualization (vīkṣaṇa). [This is the] ketanyā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, O crusher of all enemies! Hraḥ, for the weapon: Hūṃ Phaṭ!
For the purpose of marking: Khaphreṃ Oṃ, obeisance to the heart of Paramahaṃsinī.
Beholding with the eye of wisdom, *hreṃ*—the destroyer of all misfortunes, calamities, and afflictions; *hūṃ*, for the armor.

*Kusata-pūjā*. [Offering] the entire [oblation]: *Oṃ śu gāṃ gāṃ oṃ gajasarpinī śatrupramathanī hraḥ astrāya phaṭ*. [This is] the scattering of flowers. The sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) is triangular in shape.
Having drawn a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, salutations to Siddhilakṣmī Kuṇḍā. Ketaṃnya.
Hreṃ, hūṃ, homage to the armor! O you who are the mother of the three lineages!
For the purpose of marking with the Gāyatrī mantra: Oṃ, obeisance to the heart of the Supreme Haṃsinī.
*Svāna vā kuṃdasate* || *Hreṃ*, for the armor, *hūṃ*. [This is] the offering of fuel sticks (*samidh*).
*Valaṅgatahalate* || *Hraḥ astrāya phaṭ* || [The ritual] of scattering *kūśa* grass and rice concludes with the word *sakala*.
With the root mantra, [one offers] the oblation of ghee: *hrīṃ śrīṃ vāgīśvarāya svāhā*.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vāgīśvarī Svāhā. Ketaṃnya. Jaṃ, obeisance to the seat of Śakti (Jaṃ Śaktyāsanāya Namaḥ).
Svānate || Having installed the liṅga within the womb (yonimadhye) at Hasamakha phrauṁ, [it is] at Ketaṃne.
He [is] the festival of semen; at the banner, Hrīṃ Caitanya; at the banner.
Aiṁ, salutation to the heart of the Supreme Swaness; Svāhā for the rite of conception.
The invocation for the dog:
*Oṃ ju gamānāthā na riva... [savi] yāya*.
[Offering] to the dog at the fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*).
Then, having sprinkled the wood and having smeared the surface of the seat, for the purpose of drawing [the lines].
HRAḤ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ. Purification with the Gāyatrī. Siṃpaṃtane.
If one does not eat, hunger arises; if one eats, there is no hunger. If one does not drink, thirst arises; if one drinks, there is no thirst.
Oṃ, salutations to all the accomplished Yoginīs; [I worship] the venerable sandals in the center.
Salutation to all the Mothers who have attained perfection; [I offer] the venerable sandals at the southern end of the wooden [seat].
Salutation to the auspicious sandals of Nanditā, who is eternally arisen bliss; [this is] on the wooden plank in the left corner.
To the one who is the leader of the entire circle of the Kula, [I offer] the venerable sandals in front of the sacrificial pit.
Sandalwood, vermilion, incense, lamps, sacred thread, and flowers—salutations!
Khphreṃ! Having summoned the fire.
The flesh-eating fire has gone to the sacrificial offering.
Oṃ! May those beings depart who dwell upon the earth;
may those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva. Accept this offering, svāhā! Vaḥ!
Having crossed over this [world], he, as the fire of the flesh-eaters, proceeds toward the purification of the single path.
Oṃ, O subduer of all enemies, hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Phaṭ to the weapon! || ||
With an oblation of all kinds of grain, [he says]: "Svāhā to the flesh-eating Agni! || ||
One should worship with sandalwood paste and flowers; likewise, one should offer incense, lamps, and so forth, for the purpose of dismissing the fire of the flesh-eaters (kravyāgni).
HŪṂ! I release this for the flesh-eating Agni; PHAṬ to the weapon! One should cast it into the fire.
For the purification of the solar fire.
Oṃ, to the heart of the Supreme Swaness (Paramahaṃsinī).
Aiṃ Kṣīṃ, I worship the sandals of Indra... Agni... Nirṛti... Va... I worship, obeisance; I satisfy with libations, obeisance... Lānā... [I worship].
One should sprinkle [the fire] with water and mutter the mantra over the fire.
Aiṃ! We know Vaiśvānara; we meditate upon Jātavedas; may that Agni inspire us.

One should recite the mantra three times: *ketanya aundarcya vaindavadbhūta*. Having unified the three stalks (*nalatraya*) with the *vindu* and *bindu* [syllables], one should perform the recitation.
Protection with the Astra-mantra; enveloping with the Kavaca-mantra; making [it] nectar through the Dhenu-mudrā; Vaṃ.
One should rotate [the vessel] upward with the *yonimudrā*. One should worship with the sword [mudrā]. One should worship with sandalwood and other flowers.
Then, having circumambulated the fire three times.
Aiṁ Hūṁ Hūṁ Hūṁ Aiṁ Hasakhaphreṁ, I perform the establishment of the fire.
Rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ, svāhā to the consciousness of fire.
One should recite the words of auspiciousness.
May Svasti always ward off obstacles; may Svasti belong to Mārttaṇḍa alone.
(Anayaku nama vāṃ vatukāya khatuka śā pādukāṃ pūjayāmi 2 tarpayāmi 2). You are the essence of the three truths. [This is] the Sūryārgha and Nyāsa. Aṃ hṛdayāya. Arkāya śirase. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ.

Jvālinī is the crest-lock (śikhā). Hūṃ is the armor (kavaca). Bhāṃ is the eye (netra). Raṃ is the weapon (astra). Karaṃ is the placement on the hands (karanyāsa). Arghapātra, Khaḍga, and Puṣpa are the offerings (pūjā).
Self-worship. To the one without a staff. To Piṅgala.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ to Sūrya. [Offerings] such as sandalwood and so forth. Recitation: Hrāṃ svāhā. Maṇḍala.
Hymn of Praise.
Homage to Sūrya constantly; homage, again and again, to the West.
Salutation after salutation to the Āditya, the radiant light of the universe.
Here [are] the perfumes and so forth. The worship of the Sun is completed.
Worship of Gaṇeśa. Three handfuls of water (trayamjali).
Glūṃ Svāhā. Sandalwood and other offerings for Gaṇeśa. Recitation.
glūṃ svāhā ||
Hymn to the Lord of Devas.
Here ends the worship of Gaṇeśa, beginning with the offering of fragrance and the other articles.
The worship of Vaiṣṇava deities.
Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, homage to Nārāyaṇa, the soul of the universe; svāhā!
Sandalwood and so forth. Recitation: Hrīḥ svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.
To Nārāyaṇa, the Seer, the Supreme Person, the Great Soul.
Salutation to Viśveśvara, the All-pervading One, the Self of all beings.
Here ends the Vaiṣṇava worship, including the offering of perfumes and other articles.
Then follows the worship of Śiva.
Nyāsa: Hāṃ to the heart; Hīṃ to the head; Hūṃ to the crest-lock; Haiṃ to the armor.

Hauṃ for the eyes; Haṃ for the weapon. This is the ritual assignment (nyāsa) of the hands and limbs. The worship consists of the preparation of the vessel of offering (arghapātra) and the purification of the site (khaḍaṅgaṇa).
Hāṃ Hoṃ, to Sadāśiva. [The offering of] sandalwood and so forth. Japa: Hāṃ Svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.
Homage to Śiva, the peaceful one, the cause of the three causes.
[I bow] to Gaṅgā in the southeast; [I bow] to Durgā in the northwest. *Kṣāṃ* to Kṣattrakara in the northeast.
I offer myself to you, O Supreme Lord; you are my refuge.
Herein are the scents and so forth. We bow to the Triple Reality. O stainless one, you are the primordial source.
Now, the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

Oṃ. Of this Mātṛkā Nyāsa, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījas), the vowels are the powers (śaktis), the groups [of letters] are the pegs (kīlakas); its application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of one's desired goal.
Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, obeisance to the heart.
iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā to the head.
uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the tuft of hair (śikhā).
Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ, for the armor, hūṃ.
Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ luṃ kṣaṃ aḥ, phaṭ to the weapon-mantra!
Vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ || Mārggaśīrṣa.
(Naṃ | Oṃ astravaśu śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi namaḥ | Oṃ ekāda baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ || Liṅgasa ||)
Ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ || at the navel.
Kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ [to] the heart.
Aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ || To the throat: Ha Kṣaḥ, to the forehead: Aṃ, salutation. To Ca Saṃpolasa: Āṃ, salutation. To Khvārasa: Iṃ, salutation. To Javamikhāsa: [Iṃ].
Iṃ, obeisance to Khavamikhāsa. Uṃ, obeisance to Javahnasasa. Ūṃ, obeisance to Khavahnasasa. Ṛṃ, obeisance to Javahnāsaphanisa. Ṝṃ, obeisance to Khavahnāsaphanisa. Ḷṃ, obeisance to Javaṅatālasa.
Ḷṁ namaḥ to Khavaṅatālasa. Eṁ namaḥ to Kothuhmuthusisa. Aiṁ namaḥ to Thaṃthuhmuthusisa.
Oṃ, obeisance to Koṭhuvāsa. Oṃ, obeisance to Koṭhvavāsa. Aṃ, obeisance to Moṇḍadevana.

Aḥ! Homage to Meṅhana. Kaṃ! Homage to Javavohora. Khaṃ! Homage to Javacūlā. Gaṃ! Homage to Javakoṃci. Ghaṃ! Homage to Javapaṃciṅi. Ṅaṃ! Homage to Javapaṃciṅicā. Caṃ! Homage to Khavavohola. Chaṃ! Homage to...
Khavacūlāsa || Jaṃ: Homage to Khavakocisa. Jhaṃ: Homage to Khavapaṃciṅihāsa. Ñaṃ: Homage to Khavapaṃciṅicosa. Ṭaṃ: Homage to Javakalacukuli. Ṭhaṃ: Homage to Javapuḷsa. Ḍaṃ: [Homage to] Javavaṃkisa.
Ḍhaṃ, homage to Javakapisa! Ṇaṃ, homage to Javapaṃciṅilusisa! Taṃ, homage to Khavakalacukulisa!
Thaṁ namaḥ khavapu ḷ sa || Daṁ namaḥ khavavaṃki ḷ sa || Dhaṁ namaḥ khapāta ḷ sa ||
Naṃ namaḥ | Khavapaṃciṅicosa | Paṃ namaḥ khavapyaṃkosa | Phaṃ namaḥ khavavyaṃkosa | Baṃ namaḥ nābhisa | Bhaṃ namaḥ pyaṃtasa | Maṃ namaḥ luṃgvaḍaphātisa.
Yaṃ, homage to Kaṃthusu; Raṃ, homage to Javahaṃsunisa; Laṃ, homage to Milakhāsa; Vaṃ, homage to Khavahaṃsunisa;
Śaṃ, homage to Luṃgvaḍanajavalāhātatvaṃ; Ṣaṃ, homage to Nugvaḍanakhavalāhāthatvaṃ; Saṃ, homage to Nugvaḍanajavapātaḷtvaṃ.

Haṃ, obeisance to you who possess the nature of the nails of the descending [energy]. Luṃ, obeisance to you who possess the nature of the navel of the descending [energy]. Kṣaṃ, obeisance to you who possess the nature of the *brahmamukha* (the mouth of Brahmā) of the descending [energy]. These constitute the Mātṛkānyāsa.
Varivya | O venerable Lord of the Nyāsa, from all the classes of beings, accept this offering, svāhā! [Recite] "To the entire seat of mantras," and so forth.
Regarding the passage beginning with "spoken and unspoken" (*uktānukta*): Homage to Śrīnātha. Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha.

Homage to Śrīkujeśanātha. Recitation (*jāpa*), reading (*pāṭha*), hymn of praise (*stotra*), and the offering of the *samaya-chāyā* [to the deity]. Then, the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and dismissal (*visarjana*), followed by the food offering (*bali*). These are all for the daily practice.
The sandals for the body; likewise the *bali* offering; *jayādi*; *brahmāṇyādi*—these constitute the sections.
The worship of the ritual vase (kalaśapūjā).
Aiṃ, salutation to the Lotus Seat. Ha, [salutation to] Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, together with the venerable Full Jar; [to you] the sandals.
Oṃ jūṃ saḥ, the sandals for the venerable Lord Amṛtīśvara.
To Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśvara; to Amṛtīśa.
The Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, and Tuṅgabhadrā.
Śānti-kalā for Pratiṣṭhā; [perform] the invocation and so forth, and the Dhenu-mudrā. This is the worship of the Kalās.
The Worship of Gaṇapati.
Glāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Glūṃ, to Cañcalādevī together with her Śakti, accept this bali offering, svāhā! This is the worship of Gaṇapati and the bali offering.
O Ugracaṇḍā, accept this offering, svāhā!
Hskhphreṃ! O glorious Siddhicāmuṇḍā, accept this bali offering; svāhā!
Oṃ, Gaṃ! To Gaṇapati, accept this offering; Svāhā! Vāṃ! To Vaṭuka, [accept] this offering!
KṢĀṂ! To the guardian of the field, this offering! YĀṂ! To the yoginīs, accept this offering, svāhā!
Aiṃ Hūṃ! To the Great Karavīra, Lord of the Cremation Ground, accept this bali offering, svāhā!
To all the bhūtas and yoginīs, accept this bali offering; svāhā!
O you who move through the sky, accept this offering from all the spirits and yoginīs; svāhā!
The placement of the sky; breath control (prāṇāyāma); purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi); worship of the vessel (pātrapūjā); meditation (dhyāna).
Baliviya || This is the offering for the Gaṇas, Vaṭukas, Kṣetrapālas, Yoginīs, and the Mūla-mantras.
Incense, lamps, food offerings, recitation of mantras, chanting of scriptures, hymns of praise, and the observance of ritual commitments.
The dismissal of Bali is performed with this daily [offering].

Within the mandala of the venerable Samvarta, bliss is established through the stages of the steps; there is the most formidable power (śakti), the fourfold emanation according to the rule, another fivefold group pertaining to Akula and Kula, and a sixfold group.
To him who is truly joined with the mandala— consisting of four, five, and again four [deities]— bow down to that excellent Guru, Bhairava, the glorious Kujeśa.
The Flower Vessel from today onwards; salutation to the Guru; ritual placement (nyāsa); worship of the vessel (pātrapūjā).
Self-worship: Invocation, meditation, bathing with sandalwood paste and other offerings, and three handfuls of water with the root mantra.
The Palivāla-pūjā. [From] the Khaṇḍasa.
Aiṃ namaḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Caṇḍacogrā; hrīṃ, [salutation to] the sandals.
Aiṁ! That Bhairavānanda; to the venerable Ugracaṇḍā, the sovereign queen of the Great Vidyās, Ha Śrī(-), [I offer] the sandals.
The Bali offering. The worship of the Gaṇas: Aṃ Āṃ, the sandals of Rudracaṇḍā; Iṃ Iṃ, the sandals of Pracaṇḍā.
uṃ ūṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍāgrā; ṛṃ ṝṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍanāyikā; ḷṃ ḹṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍā.
Eṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍavatī. Oṃ Auṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍarūpā. Aṃ Aḥ, O Aticaṇḍī, perform the rite!
Then follows the worship on the tenth day (daśamī-pūjā), the worship of the previous deity, and the hymn of apology (kṣamā-stuti).
All the hosts of gods go forth, respectfully taking with them offerings for worship.
He is the bestower of desired objects and [the one who grants] a return.
Forgive me for all mantras, and for that which brings eternal bliss.
For the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, and for the sake of returning once more.
To Khaṇḍahlāya.
O you who stand in the fortress, you possess a sharp blade that brings about the destruction of the enemy faction.
May you be gracious; grant victory! Obeisance to you, the perfection of the sword!

The marking of the pitcher (*kalaśa*), the consecration (*abhiṣeka*), the sandalwood paste, vermilion (*siṃdūra*), and the enchanting [mantras]; the virtuous blessings; the nine nights (*navarātra*); the ritual bath (*snāna*); the offering of the water-pitcher (*kuṃbha-hlāya*); and the manner of the final dismissal (*phatasepāre*).
The seat of power is the food that pacifies.
[Thus ends the ritual procedure for the tenth offering.]
Oṃ, salutations to Caṇḍikā.
Now follows the ritual procedure for the Navarātra.
One should draw a lotus. *Phīvoya*. With the Aghora-weapon mantra, *ho*, it is sprinkled. *Phīrapoya*.
Recite the root mantra over the phāṃ-svaṃ-prāśra. *Kaleśate*. *Gvaḍajā balipāṭa te*.
Beginning with "adya" and so forth: the flower vessel; the root-mantra placement (mūla-nyāsa) of Ugracaṇḍā; the ketana.
Oṃ, salutation to Ādhāraśakti Kamalāsanā. To Ananta. To Kūrma. To Maṇḍuka.
To the Earth; to the Garden; to the Jewel Pavilion; to Ananta, the Yoga-yogapīṭha-throne.
For the lion-throne. O mind, [be] swift in the act of worship. To Laṅkhaviya. The root mantra.
Vāsa! Nandine! Bali! To Mahākāla, bali! Kṣetrapāla, bali! (*) ||
The Worship of Gaṇapati.
Glāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Glūṃ, to Cañcalādevī together with her Śakti, accept the bali offering; svāhā! (*)
Aiṃ! O Ugracaṇḍā, accept this offering; svāhā!
Aiṁ Hskhphreṁ! O Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍā, accept this bali offering; svāhā!
Aiṃ Hūṃ! To the lord of the Mahākaravīra cremation ground, accept this bali offering, svāhā!
Aiṃ! To all the yoginīs of all beings, accept this offering, svāhā!
Aiṃ! O you who move through the sky, accept this offering from all the elemental yoginīs; svāhā!
Aiṃ! To those who move through the sky and to all the [deities] of the [five] classes, [I offer] this bali. In the seat of all mantras, and so forth...
Regarding the passage beginning with "spoken and unspoken" (*uktānukta*): composed by Murabali; homage to the illustrious Lord (*śrīnātha*).
Homage to the illustrious Siddhinātha! Homage to the illustrious Kujeśanātha! (*)
The recitation of mantras and prayers for the benefit of the patron at the conclusion of the sacrifice.
The praise of Kṣamā (Forgiveness) from Khaṇḍakhādyaka. End of the section on Forgiveness. End of the Samaya.
One and many. May the Lord grant you blessings. O Mother, may what was previously attained [be yours]. May the Lord grant you blessings.
The food of the observance (*samayabhojya*). Thus is the ritual for the Great Eighth Day (*mahāṣṭamī*). These are the offerings.
There are the Navamī-pūjās for the worship of the former deities and for animal sacrifice.
The Kaumārī sacrifice, the means of accomplishment for delusion, the blessing of the deities, the dismissal of Kaumārī, and the pacification.
Thus ends the ninth worship.
Salutation to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Īśvara, Sadāśiva, and Amṛtīśa.
Salutation to the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, and Bhadrā.
Salutation to Śānti, Vidyā, Kalā, and Pratiṣṭhā. [Perform] the invocation and other rites, the Dhenu-mudrā, and the bali offering. (*)
Devīsajava || Kumbhapūjā || Aghorāṣṭaka || ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ || Rudracaṇḍādi ||
